title: 25 FOR REASONS
subtitle: A college-football poll with receipts.
question: If everybody played next Saturday, which 25 teams would we believe in most?

cadence.review: Each published edition dates its evidence and keeps the previous board.
cadence.next: Next edition after the next results review; no automatic publication is promised.

methodology.label: Strength
methodology.note: Who we would trust on a neutral field next Saturday.

methodology.label: Continuity
methodology.note: Quarterback, line, coordinator, and returning-production evidence.

methodology.label: Path
methodology.note: Schedule leverage and the real route into the 12-team playoff.

methodology.label: Accountability
methodology.note: Every case, doubt, and proof stays attached to the team all season.

sale.name: PointCast 25 / 2026 Founding Season Ticket
sale.promise: Back the complete 2026 editorial season. The ranking and its receipts remain public; the ticket funds the weekly research, audio dispatches, and permanent season ledger.

movementBaseline: Board 001 · September 23, 2026. Movement is measured from the previous published PointCast board.
editorialNote: PointCast rankings are editorial judgments. Records and latest results are from the September 27 AP poll archive; this is a September 29 review, not a live score feed.

sources.label: September 27 AP poll, records and September 26 results

teams.reason: A pressured road finish keeps Texas first.
teams.case: Winning in Knoxville with a tight fourth quarter answers last week’s travel question.
teams.doubt: Seventeen points leave an offense that still has to separate from elite defenses.
teams.proof: Turn a difficult road win into sustained scoring against another top opponent.
teams.movementReason: Board 001: #1 → #1. A pressured road finish keeps Texas first.

teams.reason: Georgia made the second chair look too small.
teams.case: A decisive result over Oklahoma is the strongest whole-game control near the top.
teams.doubt: One dominant home result does not establish the entire SEC path.
teams.proof: Carry this control into a difficult road setting.
teams.movementReason: Board 001: #2 → #2. Georgia made the second chair look too small.

teams.reason: Florida answered the question our No. 18 asked too quietly.
teams.case: A 24-point win over our No. 3 team is a serious neutral-field argument, not merely a poll jump.
teams.doubt: The defense still allowed 28; one emotional home statement is not a complete season.
teams.proof: Keep the physical edge when the opponent and venue change.
teams.movementReason: Board 001: #18 → #3. Florida answered the question our No. 18 asked too quietly.

teams.reason: A road rout keeps Notre Dame in title weather.
teams.case: The Irish handled their road assignment without turning it into a fourth-quarter negotiation.
teams.doubt: Purdue is not the strongest test on the remaining title path.
teams.proof: Show the same command against a more demanding opponent.
teams.movementReason: Board 001: #4 → #4. A road rout keeps Notre Dame in title weather.

teams.reason: The offense is loud; the defensive bill got smaller.
teams.case: A convincing SEC result makes last week’s 36 points allowed look less like a permanent condition.
teams.doubt: The next opponent can still challenge the middle of this defense.
teams.proof: Repeat the cleaner two-sided game against a ranked SEC team.
teams.movementReason: Board 001: #9 → #5. The offense is loud; the defensive bill got smaller.

teams.reason: Miami handled the assignment and waits for a sharper one.
teams.case: Four wins and a comprehensive 52–3 result preserve a credible title case.
teams.doubt: Central Michigan does not resolve the ceiling against the best teams.
teams.proof: Win a high-leverage conference game without relying on the opponent’s mistakes.
teams.movementReason: Board 001: #5 → #6. Miami handled the assignment and waits for a sharper one.

teams.reason: The champion survived; the margin invites a harder look.
teams.case: The unbeaten record and prior continuity still matter when a conference game tightens.
teams.doubt: Northwestern staying within six makes automatic title trust harder to defend.
teams.proof: Create separation against the next quality opponent.
teams.movementReason: Board 001: #6 → #7. The champion survived; the margin invites a harder look.

teams.reason: Ohio State is moving from reputation toward repair.
teams.case: A 23-point conference win shows the post-loss adjustment is taking shape.
teams.doubt: One loss and a home response still leave the road version uncertain.
teams.proof: Take this defensive and offensive balance to Iowa.
teams.movementReason: Board 001: #7 → #8. Ohio State is moving from reputation toward repair.

teams.reason: The response to Oxford was emphatic.
teams.case: Holding Texas A&M to six and winning by 29 is more useful than asking everyone to forget Ole Miss.
teams.doubt: A&M had already lost at home to Kentucky, which limits the size of the inference.
teams.proof: Repeat the defensive control against an opponent with a stronger recent résumé.
teams.movementReason: Board 001: #11 → #9. The response to Oxford was emphatic.

teams.reason: BYU keeps its place while the live evidence catches up.
teams.case: An unbeaten 3–0 foundation and the earlier road win survive an idle week.
teams.doubt: A week off supplies no new proof against the teams now rising around it.
teams.proof: Win the next demanding Big 12 game on the field.
teams.movementReason: Board 001: #8 → #10. BYU keeps its place while the live evidence catches up.

teams.reason: The scoreboard finally supplied separation.
teams.case: A 35-point win is a better follow-up to the Houston escape than another narrow finish.
teams.doubt: Sam Houston is not the toughest test in this tier.
teams.proof: Turn the same scoring margin into control against a Big 12 contender.
teams.movementReason: Board 001: #10 → #11. The scoreboard finally supplied separation.

teams.reason: Oxford counted; Gainesville set its limit.
teams.case: The LSU win remains evidence that the Rebels can beat a strong opponent.
teams.doubt: The first road game produced a 24-point loss and directly failed last board’s next proof.
teams.proof: Respond away from home against a credible opponent with four-quarter composure.
teams.movementReason: Board 001: #3 → #12. Oxford counted; Gainesville set its limit.

teams.reason: The road surprise now has a home follow-up.
teams.case: Beating Missouri after winning at South Carolina gives the ascent a second SEC result.
teams.doubt: A seven-point home margin leaves the defensive floor open to challenge.
teams.proof: Keep the unbeaten run through a higher-ranked opponent.
teams.movementReason: Board 001: #22 → #13. The road surprise now has a home follow-up.

teams.reason: The repair job has a road receipt.
teams.case: A two-touchdown win at USC is the quality result the July No. 4 argument lacked.
teams.doubt: The earlier loss remains on the record, and 27 conceded is not complete control.
teams.proof: Repeat the road quality against another conference heavyweight.
teams.movementReason: Board 001: #20 → #14. The repair job has a road receipt.

teams.reason: Utah keeps building its floor on the road.
teams.case: An unbeaten start and a two-touchdown Big 12 road win make the post-Whittingham transition look sturdier.
teams.doubt: The highest offensive ceiling still needs a more severe test.
teams.proof: Beat a contender without losing that defensive discipline.
teams.movementReason: Board 001: #13 → #15. Utah keeps building its floor on the road.

teams.reason: The last play made the road argument real.
teams.case: An unbeaten record and a one-point win in Ann Arbor deserve credit for composure.
teams.doubt: One point is also how close the result was to turning the other way.
teams.proof: Give Ohio State a full-game test, not only a memorable finish.
teams.movementReason: Board 001: #17 → #16. The last play made the road argument real.

teams.reason: The loss to No. 1 still carries useful evidence.
teams.case: A three-point home loss to Texas showed Tennessee can force an elite opponent to solve it late.
teams.doubt: The offense scored only 17 and did not finish the upset.
teams.proof: Turn competitive pressure into a win against another ranked opponent.
teams.movementReason: Board 001: #15 → #17. The loss to No. 1 still carries useful evidence.

teams.reason: Houston made the close loss look less accidental.
teams.case: The two-point loss at Texas Tech now sits beside a 14-point road response.
teams.doubt: Georgia Southern does not confirm top-tier Big 12 strength.
teams.proof: Beat a conference opponent with cleaner defensive control.
teams.movementReason: Board 001: #25 → #18. Houston made the close loss look less accidental.

teams.reason: The defensive bill came due against Oregon.
teams.case: Four earlier wins still give USC a plausible conference path.
teams.doubt: Forty-one conceded at home confirms the doubt attached to Board 001.
teams.proof: Hold a quality Big Ten offense below its preferred tempo and win.
teams.movementReason: Board 001: #12 → #19. The defensive bill came due against Oregon.

teams.reason: SMU steadied the record without closing the case.
teams.case: A ten-point win after the Louisville loss keeps the Mustangs in the conversation.
teams.doubt: Missouri State cannot settle the ranked-opponent question.
teams.proof: Beat an ACC contender on both sides of the ball.
teams.movementReason: Board 001: #23 → #20. SMU steadied the record without closing the case.

teams.reason: Kentucky’s A&M win deserves a seat at this table.
teams.case: A decisive follow-up gives the Texas A&M road upset continuity.
teams.doubt: The latest opponent does not prove the same level of SEC repeatability.
teams.proof: Get a second conference win that stands on its own.
teams.movementReason: New to Board 002 after the September 26 results. Kentucky’s A&M win deserves a seat at this table.

teams.reason: An unbeaten road rout earns a first PointCast look.
teams.case: A 51-point win away from home is hard to leave outside the conversation.
teams.doubt: The schedule has not yet supplied a ranked opponent.
teams.proof: Show the same structure against a strong Big Ten team.
teams.movementReason: New to Board 002 after the September 26 results. An unbeaten road rout earns a first PointCast look.

teams.reason: A road win makes the comeback visible.
teams.case: Three straight victories and a 17-point Big 12 road result support a new entry.
teams.doubt: The earlier loss and quality of opposition keep this in the fault-line group.
teams.proof: Defeat a top-half Big 12 opponent without a fourth-quarter rescue.
teams.movementReason: New to Board 002 after the September 26 results. A road win makes the comeback visible.

teams.reason: The first loss narrows Missouri’s opening claim.
teams.case: The unbeaten opening still gave Missouri a usable base before Starkville.
teams.doubt: Losing the first consequential SEC comparison leaves the ceiling in doubt.
teams.proof: Answer the loss with a ranked-conference win.
teams.movementReason: Board 001: #21 → #24. The first loss narrows Missouri’s opening claim.

teams.reason: The Broncos return with a credible road margin.
teams.case: Three straight wins after the Oregon loss include a 25-point road result.
teams.doubt: The schedule still needs a stronger proof than Western Michigan.
teams.proof: Win a game that tests the Group of Six ceiling directly.
teams.movementReason: New to Board 002 after the September 26 results. The Broncos return with a credible road margin.
